**Summary:**

The internet originated in the 1960s as a US Department of Defense project, with ARPANET demonstrating the first network message in 1969, and the adoption of TCP/IP protocols in 1983 establishing the foundation for the modern internet. Tim Berners-Lee's invention of the World Wide Web in 1989 and the release of the Mosaic browser in 1993 made the internet accessible to ordinary users, leading to explosive growth during the dot-com boom of the late 1990s. The subsequent dot-com crash in 2001 eliminated many companies, though survivors like Amazon and Google became highly valuable, while the 2007 iPhone launch and AWS (2006) further transformed the landscape through mobile access and cloud computing. Today, over 5 billion people are connected, with the internet now underpinning virtually every aspect of modern life.
